question: For every human cell in a typical adult body, roughly how many bacterial cells are there?
answer: About 1. A 2016 recount put a 70 kg man at roughly 38 trillion bacteria and 30 trillion human cells, most of those red blood cells. The famous ten-to-one came from a 1972 back-of-envelope estimate. The two are so close that a single bowel movement can tip the balance towards human.
move: A figure repeated everywhere may trace back to one rough guess.
trap: Recalling the widely quoted ten bacteria for every human cell.
reference: Sender, Fuchs & Milo, Revised estimates for the number of human and bacteria cells in the body, PLoS Biology, 2016
